title: VALUE LEAKAGE: AN LLM'S ANSWERS ARE SILENTLY SHAPED BY ITS OWN VALUES

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual prompts asking for Fermi estimates where the model is told that an answer above or below a specific threshold will trigger a donation to a good or bad cause.

Counterfactual prompts mentioning the model's creator company versus a competitor in various scenarios, including AI bubble forecasts, AGI timeline predictions, career advice, and agentic grading of text responses.

Asking models to randomly choose between pairs of leisure activities (sometimes using external tools like a coin flip or Unix time) and measuring the correlation between selection rates and the model's stated preferences.
Evaluating whether an LLM grader disproportionately favors text answers that are labeled as being generated by more capable models (e.g., GPT-4o vs. GPT-4o-mini) during an agentic grading task.

Measuring agentic effort (persistence) by counting the number of times a model retries a failing money transfer tool, depending on the identity of the recipient (e.g., a favored charity versus a political party).
